who: Historian of contemporary art and visual semiotics at Université Laval.

evidence.says: The 1995 contributor biography identifies Marie Carani as a contemporary art historian and visual semiologist teaching history at Université Laval.
The Marie Carani authority cites her contribution to Lieux/parcours Michel Labbé 1988.
The art-library bibliography groups Lieux/Parcours; Michel Labbé, 1988 with Carani’s art-history publications, including Jean-Paul Lemieux and De l’histoire de l’art à la sémiotique visuelle.

notes: The authority’s art publications and the contemporary Laval affiliation agree with the supervisor’s field and period. Direct confirmation in Poiré’s thesis was not obtained.

who: Historian of early modern France, professor at Université Laval; retired in 2010.

evidence.says: Pages 20–21 identify historian Claire Dolan as a retired professor of historical sciences, discuss her Laval career and history department directorship, and date her retirement to 2010.
The publisher identifies Claire Dolan as an associate professor of historical sciences at Laval, with research on sixteenth-century Provence and seventeenth-century Toulouse.
The Claire Dolan authority identifies her as the author of Entre Tours et Clochers (1981), a historical work on Aix-en-Provence.

notes: The Laval historian’s career and early modern French field match. The alternative C. Terrence Dolan heading is not the supervisor’s name.

who: Historian of Mexico and Yucatán at Université Laval; doctoral co-advisor of Catherine Vézina.

evidence.says: The licensed book preview’s acknowledgements identify Marie Lapointe as Vézina’s doctoral co-advisor and mention Bernard Lemelin of Université Laval.
The publisher preview identifies Marie Lapointe’s affiliation as Université Laval in her chapter on twentieth-century Mexican history.
The Marie Lapointe authority cites Los mayas rebeldes de Yucatán (1983).
The university’s review identifies historian Marie Lapointe as the author of both Los mayas rebeldes de Yucatán and Histoire du Yucatan.

notes: Advisor acknowledgement, Laval affiliation, and Mexican-history publications agree. The other candidates have different compound given names.

who: Philosophy professor at St. Thomas More College, University of Saskatchewan; later at Emory; PhD Dalhousie 1980.

evidence.says: The winter 1998/99 college newsletter says Kevin Corrigan joined its philosophy department in 1986 and served as dean from 1991 to 1998; it mentions his education at Dalhousie.
The authority identifies the author of Plotinus’ theory of matter as Emory professor Kevin Corrigan, with a Dalhousie PhD in classics and philosophy (1980).
The other Kevin Corrigan authority identifies an actor and writer through the film Walking and Talking.

notes: The philosopher’s Saskatchewan appointment covers Fitzgerald’s 1996 doctorate; the actor candidate is a different person. The thesis supervision itself was not independently confirmed.

who: Scholar of military policy and nuclear history; Carnegie Mellon history assistant professor, 1987–1990; PhD sociology, Michigan 1985.

evidence.says: Her Stanford-hosted CV lists Carnegie Mellon history employment in 1987–1990, a Michigan sociology PhD in 1985, and the books Whole World on Fire and Nuclear Arguments.
The Lynn Eden authority cites Whole World on Fire and identifies Nuclear Arguments among her works.

notes: The authority’s books identify the scholar whose Carnegie Mellon appointment and military-policy field fit Hogan’s dissertation. She moved to Stanford before the recorded 1991 completion.

who: Professor of history at State University of New York at Binghamton, publishing on international affairs in the 1970s.

evidence.says: A 1975 American Journal of International Law correspondence identifies Laurence Evans as professor of history at SUNY Binghamton.
The L. K. Evans candidate is expanded as Lewis K. Evans and is associated with Pioneer History of Greene County, Pennsylvania.
The L. S. Evans candidate is Lee S. Evans, associated with Selecting Engineering Materials for Chemical and Process Plant.
The L. Evans candidate is Lionel Evans, associated with Psychology and Communication in Deaf Children.

notes: All 13 supplied LC records were checked. Their expanded names are Lewis, Linda, Lauren, Laurynn, Lee, Lionel, Louis, or Lynda; none identifies Laurence Evans, the Binghamton history professor.

who: David M. Farquhar, historian of China, Mongolia and Inner Asia; Maryland history faculty before moving to UCLA in 1964.

evidence.says: The Maryland repository thesis, printed pages 53–54, identifies David Farquhar as a history assistant professor specializing in Mongolia and Inner Asia who left in 1964; its biographical citation names David M. Farquhar.

The David M. Farquhar authority gives the fuller name David Miller Farquhar, cites The Ch’ing Administration of Mongolia and The Government of China under Mongolian Rule, and records UCLA premodern Chinese history employment from 1964.
The other prominent David Farquhar heading identifies a composer and music professor at Victoria University of Wellington.

notes: The Maryland-to-UCLA career and Chinese-history field identify nr92017891. His 1964 departure precedes Wu’s recorded 1965 completion, consistent with supervision before the move; Wu’s thesis was not independently checked.

who: Professor of folklore and English at Arkansas State University since 2002; PhD folklore, Indiana University 2001.

evidence.says: His university CV lists an Indiana folklore PhD (2001), Arkansas State employment since 2002, and authorship of A Florida Fiddler: The Life and Times of Richard Seaman (2007).
The Gregory Hansen authority is established from A Florida Fiddler (2007).
Hansen’s Folklore and Oral History within Heritage Studies identifies his Arkansas State affiliation and describes the university’s interdisciplinary doctoral Heritage Studies program.

notes: The exact book links the authority to the Arkansas State professor, whose appointment covers Guillory’s 2016 dissertation and whose heritage-studies work fits its subject.
